channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Marni Jenkins Visual Art Prize 2026 · CALYX Press
item.description: CALYX Press, the oldest feminist press in the United States, has launched the inaugural Marni Jenkins Visual Art Prize, a blind competition with a rotating final judge for work by women and nonbinary artists. The winner receives a $400 cash prize and publication in an upcoming issue of CALYX, A Journal of Art and Literature by Women+, the press's biannual print publication, whose every issue carries a glossy full-colour insert of visual art. The winner and up to two runners-up are published on calyxpress.org and receive a complimentary one-volume subscription of three issues - though the press's own contest page words this more broadly, saying the winner and all finalists get the subscription and the website publication. This year's final judge is Betty LaDuke, an Ashland, Oregon painter whose shaped and painted wood panels address social justice, food security and cultural diversity, and whose work is held by the Portland Art Museum, the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art, the Hallie Ford Museum of Art and the Oregon State Capitol. The prize is named for Meredith 'Marni' Jenkins, a founding member of CALYX Press and an accomplished photographer and painter, and it exists to encourage bold new visual art that challenges convention and explores the broad experiences and perspectives of women and nonbinary artists. The submission window runs 1 July to 30 November 2026. Submit up to six pieces of visual art; photographs of three-dimensional work such as sculpture and textile pieces are welcome, and the CALYX editorial collective reads everything first before sending twenty finalists to the judge. Files must be JPG or PNG, at least 300 dpi and at least five inches wide at that resolution, in RGB or CMYK. Work must be unpublished, and simultaneous submissions are discouraged. CALYX operates a strict anti-AI policy and asks that no work generated with AI tools be submitted. Entry is through Submittable at $15, which the press's own page itemises as a $14 consideration fee plus a $1 PayPal processing fee. Winners are announced in January 2027. Note that CALYX also takes free year-round art submissions on a separate track, considered by its Art Collective each May and December. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $400 + Publication.

item.title: 22nd Annual Small Works Show 2026 · 440 Gallery
item.description: 440 Gallery, an artist-run cooperative in Park Slope, Brooklyn, is taking entries for the 22nd edition of its annual Small Works Show, a national juried exhibition celebrating artists who work at a small scale across a broad range of media and styles. The 2026 edition is juried by Constanza Valenzuela, a New York curator, writer and cultural producer who is Associate Curator at Powerhouse Arts in Brooklyn, where she runs the rotating exhibition programme and leads the Artist in Residence and Artist Subsidy programmes that distribute more than $150,000 a year in fabrication support. She was previously Assistant Curator at the High Line and has worked at Creative Time, Swiss Institute, 80WSE, the New York Foundation for the Arts and El Museo del Barrio, and has curated at The Shed, CUE Art Foundation, Canal Projects and Pratt. The selected show runs at 440 Sixth Avenue from 27 November to 20 December 2026, with an opening reception on 5 December. Photography is named outright in the eligible media, alongside oils, acrylics, watercolours, pastels, drawings, sculpture in any medium, collage, printmaking and digital media, and any subject matter is welcome. Work must be no more than 12 inches in any direction including framing or mounting, a limit the gallery says will be strictly enforced; video works must run no longer than a minute and are entered with a still image plus an emailed link. Judging is from JPEGs only, one megabyte maximum per image. The call is open to artists 18 or over with a US shipping address. Entry is $25 for the first work, $10 each for works two to five and $5 each thereafter up to ten works, so ten pieces cost $90. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 40 per cent commission; no price-on-request listings are accepted. Results go out on 15 and 16 October. Accepted work is hand-delivered on 21 or 22 November, or shipped to arrive on 19 or 20 November with a prepaid return label enclosed. — Deadline: September 9, 2026. Fee: $25–$90 (1–10 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SOLO 2027 · Bromfield Gallery
item.description: Bromfield Gallery, founded in 1975 and one of Boston's oldest artist-run galleries, runs SOLO as an annual competition awarding two solo exhibitions with all gallery expenses paid. It is aimed squarely at artists who have not yet had a solo show in a commercial gallery anywhere - group shows, university galleries, libraries, frame shops, cafes and community centres do not disqualify - and all media are welcome. The 2027 juror is Shey Rivera Ríos, Artistic Director of the Boston Center for the Arts, an interdisciplinary artist, cultural worker and curator with a fifteen-year record in arts and community development who serves on the Arts Policy Committee for Grantmakers in the Arts. Entry is $35 for five JPEGs, ideally a recent coherent body of work representing the exhibition you would mount. Finalists are asked to bring three to five pieces of current work to the gallery in October for review by the juror, all entrants are emailed the result, and winners are posted on the gallery website by 1 December. The two winning exhibitions are held in January 2027. The gallery pays the exhibition costs - postcard, exhibition fee, reception and so on - while artists remain responsible for making their work and for travel or shipping; all work in the exhibition must be for sale. Eligibility is limited to the six New England states, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont, and your primary residence must be in New England from the application deadline through 31 January, the end of the exhibition period. Applications are accepted only through Submittable. Bromfield is in Boston's SoWa district at 450 Harrison Avenue, alongside two dozen contemporary galleries and the Boston Center for the Arts. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Flourish Fund 2026–27 · CultureSource
item.description: The Flourish Fund is CultureSource's regranting programme for Southeast Michigan, run in partnership with the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts as part of its Regional Regranting Program. It awards six grants of $10,000 each, every year, to artist-organised projects that are experimental and risk-taking, collaborative, shared with the public, and rooted in a visual arts practice. Projects can be interdisciplinary but must have a strong foundation in the visual arts, and the fund states that proposals may span mediums and disciplines from sculpture to projection mapping, printmaking to immersive technology, and beyond; recent grantees include a Detroit community-archiving project built on pop-up digitisation events for family photographs and home movies, paired with contemporary artists' work in galleries and installations. Applicants must be independent, unincorporated artists at any career stage, and the lead organiser must live in one of the seven Southeast Michigan counties - Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw, Monroe, Livingston or St Clair - with the project taking place and being publicly shared in one of them. Groups and collectives may apply with a single lead applicant, who receives the funds. Projects run by incorporated entities including LLCs and 501(c)(3)s, by universities, schools, religious institutions or municipalities, or led by currently enrolled high school or university students, are not eligible, and the fund does not support retroactive or reimbursement requests. The application asks for artist and project information, work samples, a proposed budget and several short answers, and is free to enter through Submittable. Applications opened on 13 August and close on Friday 11 September 2026; note that the portal stays open until 11.59pm but technical assistance ends at 5pm. An independent committee including previous Flourish Fund grantees reviews and ranks proposals, then meets to agree the six awards, with notification to all applicants in mid-October. Grantees receive $6,000 on signing and $3,000 at the interim report stage. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Lightning Fund 2027 · Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions
item.description: LACE, Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions, has opened the seventh edition of its Lightning Fund, an annual regranting programme supported by the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts. This cycle it awards ten artist project grants of $6,000 each to artists and artist-run collectives, projects and publications in Los Angeles County. The same application also decides the Jacki Apple Award, a $10,000 grant to one LA-based mid- or advanced-career artist for work resulting in a performance, media project, exhibition or publication within a year; no separate application is needed. LACE describes its definition of visual art practice as expansive, listing drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, installation and similar mediums alongside film and video, new media, sound art, performance art and social practice; practices firmly rooted in dance, theatre, music or industry, feature and documentary filmmaking are not eligible, nor are nonprofit organisations and LLCs set up for commercial enterprise. Applicants must live in Los Angeles County, be at least 18, and not be currently enrolled in a college programme. Proposals should be innovative and socially relevant and accessible to the public outside traditional museum or gallery settings, and the review prioritises presentations in Los Angeles County; awarded projects are not intended to be shown at LACE. Previous winners may reapply after waiting two cycles. The application asks for contact details, a 300-word account of your practice and past projects, and a 500-word project description covering timeline, collaborators, materials, location and needs. Entry is free, through Submittable. Applications opened on 12 August and close on 23 September 2026 at 11.59pm PST, a deadline LACE describes as firm; decisions and funds follow by the end of January 2027. A recorded information session is posted on the LACE website. — Deadline: September 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: Ursa Major Fund · Bunnell Street Arts Center
item.description: The Ursa Major Fund is Alaska's Andy Warhol Foundation Regional Regranting programme, administered by Bunnell Street Arts Center in Homer. It makes ten grants of $6,000 each to Alaska artists and artist collectives for artist-led, risk-taking, public-facing projects that inspire curiosity, engagement, dialogue and respect for cultural integrity. Funded projects should take place in Alaska, be led by Alaska artists and be intended for Alaska audiences, must be artist-organised and artist-initiated, must include a public-facing component that is free and open to participants, and should be completed within the calendar year of the award. Projects that form part of a nonprofit's or a business's own programming, that are part of an MFA or BFA course, that lack a free public component, or that take place at Bunnell Street Arts Center itself are not funded. Eligibility runs to artists and culture bearers over 18 who define Alaska as home; artists with an LLC may apply, 501(c)(3)s and for-profit businesses such as galleries may not, and MFA or BFA students may collaborate but not lead. A valid social security number is needed to receive payment. The application window opens on 1 September and closes on 15 October each year, with office hours available throughout and statewide Zoom information sessions in August and September. A jury drawn primarily from outside Alaska adjudicates on artistic excellence, community impact and feasibility during November and December; grantees are notified on 31 December, sign agreements by 15 January, receive 80 per cent of the award by 31 January and the balance on filing a project summary the following December. Entry is free, through Submittable. The first cohort, announced for 2026, funded work ranging from a mobile art trailer touring Alaskan communities to an online glacier archive, a Tlingit spruce-root weaving exhibition and arts programming for villages served by the Selawik National Wildlife Refuge. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: Into The Woods · Mosaic Art Collective
item.description: Mosaic Art Collective in Manchester, New Hampshire is taking entries for Into The Woods, an autumn and Halloween themed group exhibition. The collective is looking for art that celebrates autumn - the landscape, the people, the activities, the holidays and the emotions of the season - and says broad interpretations of the theme are welcome. Work in all mediums may apply, with reproductions and AI-generated work excluded. Entry is $10 for the first piece and $10 for each additional one, up to four entries, so a full submission costs $40. Submissions close on Friday 25 September 2026 at 11.59pm and acceptances go out on Sunday 27 September. The show hangs at the collective's gallery at 410 Chestnut Street from 10 October to 1 November 2026, opening with a reception on 10 October from 5 to 7pm. Work is dropped off in person on 30 September, 1 October or 2 October between 4 and 6pm and collected on 4, 5 or 6 November in the same window, which in practice makes this a call for artists who can reach Manchester. Sales are not guaranteed, but when they happen the artist keeps 75 per cent and the collective retains 25 per cent. All work must arrive ready to hang with proper hanging wire; there is a $5 wiring fee at drop-off if yours is not wired, and uncollected work incurs a $10 a day storage charge. Mosaic's exhibitions committee reserves the right to decline work that does not fit the theme or the technical and presentation requirements. There is no cash award; the return is the exhibition. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $10–$40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Ray and Nancy Loeschner Art Competition 2026 · Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park
item.description: Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park in Grand Rapids, Michigan runs the Ray and Nancy Loeschner Art Competition annually for two-dimensional art and photography inspired by its gardens, grounds and collections. Two purchase awards of $5,000 each are made, one for two-dimensional work and one, running under its own name since 2018, for photography; both winning entries are acquired into the institution's permanent collection. Colour, black and white, analogue film and digital photographs are all accepted, and photographers have taken the photography award every year on record - Cari Povenz in 2025, Annemarie Biernacki in 2024, Sara Kani in 2023, Laurie Tennent in 2022, Lynn Strough in 2021. The competition is open to all artists aged 18 and over. You do not have to visit Meijer Gardens to enter; artists are welcome to work on site but may equally take their inspiration from photographs and videos of the place. Entry is free. There is a two-step process: the first round is digital, with a one-page resume, a one-page artist statement explaining how the work is inspired by Meijer Gardens (required for the work to be juried), and images no smaller than 1024 x 768 at 72 dpi, with the dimensions given - print size for photographic entries. A maximum of three entries per artist is allowed. Second-round finalists deliver or ship their original work to Meijer Gardens for judging, and a finalist in the photography category must have their photograph printed for the judges. Submissions opened on 1 September and close at 11.59pm EST on Tuesday 1 December 2026; finalists are notified in December, the finalists are juried in January 2027 and winners are notified in February 2027. Judging is by a panel of Meijer Gardens professional staff and trustees. Digital artwork is accepted in the two-dimensional category but the competition states that AI use of any kind is not accepted. Winning images may be reproduced on posters and note cards with full credit but without further royalties, and previous winners may not enter again. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2 × $5,000 purchase awards.

item.title: Stone Canoe Visual Art Submissions
item.description: Stone Canoe is an annual print journal of arts, literature and ideas from Upstate New York, founded at Syracuse University in 2007 and now published by the Downtown Writers Center at the Arts Branch of the YMCA of Central New York. It appears each February and carries fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, short plays and a substantial visual art section. Photography is explicitly among the work it publishes: the guidelines say any type of visual art is considered and list sculpture, ceramic, photography, drawing, quilts, jewellery, installation views and video stills among the types that have appeared, and note that dimensions are not required for photographs where the print size is variable. Visual art submissions are free and limited to five images, each uploaded separately so that titles and details stay matched to the right picture, with a caption for each in the form artist name, title, medium and materials, dimensions and year completed - the caption appears in the printed book exactly as submitted. A biographical note documenting your Upstate New York residency must accompany every image. The one hard eligibility rule is that Stone Canoe publishes only writers and artists who live or have lived in Upstate New York, defined as the state outside New York City and Long Island; qualifying connections are read generously and include being born in the region even if you left, studying at an upstate institution, or having worked there at any point, and the work itself can be about anything at all and need not involve New York State. Previously published work, including in online journals, is not accepted, and simultaneous submissions must be withdrawn if placed elsewhere. The reading period runs from 1 April, and visual art closes on 15 September for the issue published the following spring. Editors aim to respond by mid-November. Stone Canoe also offers sponsor-funded cash prizes to emerging artists and writers with no entry fee or separate application, among them the Hedy and Michael Fawcett Prize for Visual Art; the journal cautions that its prizes depend on sponsors and may be altered or cancelled, and its published record shows the visual art prize last awarded for issue #12. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 2026 Looking Through the Lens Juried Exhibition · Medford Arts Center
item.description: An open photography exhibition at the Medford Arts Center in New Jersey, shown online and - for artists who can hand-deliver - in the gallery at 8 N. Main Street. The 2026 edition runs 2 October to 5 November, with an awards reception on Friday 2 October from 6 to 8pm. Bill Horin is Juror of Awards and the show is chaired by Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Entry is open to artists 18 and older, who may submit up to three pieces; the prospectus heads the show an Open Photography Exhibit and the Center's own listing says all media of that work are accepted, provided it is family friendly. Work must be original, conceived and signed by the artist, and must not have been shown at MAC before. This is juried for acceptance - not everything entered gets in, and only accepted work appears in the online exhibit. Accepted artists who can deliver in person on 30 September (2-4pm) or 1 October (4-6pm) also have the option of hanging in the gallery, framed and wired with no sawtooth hangers; all accepted work goes into a downloadable brochure, a YouTube video and the Center's online shop. Fees are $30 for one piece, $40 for two and $50 for three, with MAC members paying $20, $30 and $40. Awards are given by the Center's listing to first and second place plus three honorable mentions, and by the prospectus to first, second and third place plus three honorable mentions; no amount is published on either. All work must be for sale, the Center takes a 30% commission, and artists are responsible for shipping sold work to the buyer. Notification is by email on 29 September. The Medford Arts Center is a 501(c)(3) non-profit; this edition is funded in part by a grant from the Burlington County Board of Commissioners, a partner of the New Jersey State Council on the Arts. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $30 first piece, $40 for two, $50 for three (MAC members $20/$30/$40). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Selected Exhibitions Program · Capture Photography Festival
item.description: Capture Photography Festival's Selected Exhibitions Program is the juried core of its April festival in Vancouver. Rather than mounting shows itself, Capture selects independently organised lens-based exhibitions and folds them into a month-long, city-wide programme; the 2027 festival runs 1-30 April. Applications are open from 8 September to 18 October 2026 at 11:59pm PST, for exhibitions presented in galleries and informal spaces during April 2027. You do not have to be Vancouver-based to apply and you can apply as an independent artist, but the exhibition must take place in Metro Vancouver during at least part of April and a confirmed venue is required at the point of submission - if the space is not your own, Capture asks for a confirmation letter from the venue plus an exhibition floorplan as a single PDF. The festival is explicit that it cannot provide venues, and points applicants at community galleries, retail spaces, empty storefronts, libraries and universities, or their own studio. The 2027 jury is Dr. Curtis Collins (Executive Director, Audain Art Museum), artist Michelle Sound, curator and arts administrator Gaetane Verna, and Emmy Lee Wall (Executive Director and Chief Curator, Capture); they are looking for proposals presenting primarily lens-based work of artistic excellence across a diverse range of subject matter. A submission takes exhibition and venue details, artist and curator bios, and up to seven images at 300 dpi with a PDF of credits naming each work's specific medium - scans of negatives, transparencies, photographic prints and digital renderings are all accepted, and unfinished work is not. The fee is $20, which includes a 2027/2028 Capture Photography Festival Society membership; the festival invites anyone for whom the fee is a barrier, or who is already a member, to write for a waiver. Selected exhibitions receive a full page in the Capture Catalogue distributed free across Greater Vancouver, a webpage with up to seven images on the festival site, priority coverage on Capture's social channels, a Capture logo vinyl for the venue, the chance to join festival programming such as gallery hops, and a one-year membership. There is no cash award and no production funding. The separate Events Program - talks, screenings, tours, workshops - is free to enter, is not jury-evaluated, and opens early in 2027. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: CA$20 (includes a 2027/2028 Capture membership; waivers on request). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Generator Fund 2026 — Kinetic & Potential Grants · Buffalo Institute for Contemporary Art
item.description: The Generator Fund is the Buffalo Institute for Contemporary Art's regranting programme, launched in August 2023 as part of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program, and it puts $60,000 in grants into the hands of artists living and working in Erie and Niagara Counties, New York. It has awarded over 50 grants since 2023, supporting exhibitions, performances, workshops, publications, gardens, sound works and new artist-run spaces. Cycle 4 offers two grant types on one deadline. Kinetic Grants of up to $5,000 fund an artist's production for a new short-term project with a publicly accessible component - exhibitions, performances, videos or film screenings, books, zines or brochures. Potential Grants of up to $10,000 act as seed funding for longer-term, platform-building work: exhibition spaces from formal to informal, podcasts or radio stations, zines or forums for arts writing, collective spaces, community gardens, public lecture series. You may apply as lead applicant for both, as long as each proposal is distinct. Photography is named outright in the fund's own list of eligible media, alongside painting, sculpture, installation, printmaking, video, performance art, social practice and zines; work rooted primarily in music, theatre, dance, creative writing or film without a clear visual arts framework is not eligible. Applicants must live and work in Erie or Niagara County and may apply as an individual artist, an informal group or an unincorporated collective - 501(c)(3) organisations, BICA employees and anyone receiving a BICA solo exhibition honorarium in the same fiscal year cannot. There is no application fee. A venue does not need to be locked down at the point of applying, and the fund actively encourages artist stipends: you can pay yourself, collaborators, assistants, materials, travel and rentals out of the grant. Funded projects generally cannot take place at BICA itself, and must be publicly accessible somewhere in Erie or Niagara County. Projects cannot start before 1 January 2027 and must be completed by 31 December 2027. The Cycle 4 jury is H Boone, Megan Lee, Zack Boehler and Julio César Morales, who are asked to read applications with generosity and curiosity rather than looking for the most polished grant writers. Applications go through Submittable with a project description, a budget on the fund's own template, work samples and a CV; grantees are notified in December 2026 and first cheques go out in January 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $10,000.

item.title: 2026 Visual Arts Fund · Midway Contemporary Art
item.description: Open only to artists based in the seven-county Twin Cities metro region of Minnesota. The Visual Arts Fund is Midway Contemporary Art's regranting programme, established in 2016 with support from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, which makes Minneapolis-Saint Paul one of forty-two cities and regions in the Foundation's Regional Regranting Program. In 2026 the fund awards $60,000 as six grants of $10,000 to artist-organised projects. Proposals must name a lead organizer who plays a key role in creating and executing the work and who lives in Hennepin, Scott, Ramsey, Dakota, Anoka, Carver or Washington County; collaborators can live anywhere, individuals or groups may apply, and lead organizers do not need to be US citizens although they need a social security number to be paid. Projects must have a publicly accessible component taking place within the metro region, cannot charge admission or any fee to the public or to participants, and must function primarily within a visual arts context rather than performing arts, music or literature - interdisciplinary elements are fine if the visual arts basis is strong. Examples the fund gives include exhibitions or installations in temporary spaces, new publications, series of events or performances, digital initiatives and public art projects. What it will not fund is an individual artist presenting exclusively their own work, projects that form part of a 501(c)(3)'s programming, projects at a commercial gallery, and anything without free public engagement. 501(c)(3)s, incorporated businesses and students cannot apply, though PhD students can. Photography is fundable and the fund's own grantee archive proves it: Sho Nikaido's BlueSky Photo Workshop received $10,000 for four seasonal, six-week community photography courses held in Japanese restaurants across the Twin Cities. Applications are free, filed through Midway's own portal, and take contact details, a project summary and budget, ten visual support materials (up to ten images, two website URLs and two two-minute videos), a project description answering eight set questions, and bios. A panel of outside jurors scores on artistic excellence, community impact and feasibility. Projects cannot start before 1 January 2027 and must be completed by 30 June 2028; grantees are notified in December 2026 and funding is awarded in January 2027. — Deadline: September 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: 2026 Betsy Meyer Memorial Exhibition & Meyer Family Award · Main Line Art Center
item.description: Main Line Art Center's annual Betsy Meyer Memorial Exhibition and Meyer Family Award for Contemporary Art honours three artists a year with a show in the Center's gallery in Haverford, Pennsylvania, and an award of $1,000. The programme exists to support and honour contemporary artists and to encourage excellence and experimentation in artistic practice, presentation and community involvement. The 2026 exhibition runs 14 November to 18 December, opening with a reception and artist talks on Saturday 14 November from 6 to 8pm. All fine artists are eligible to apply, all mediums are welcome - the organiser's own Artwork Archive listing names photography among the accepted categories - and artists are encouraged to submit work that pushes the boundaries of their medium. The practical conditions are strict and worth reading before applying. Everything you apply with must be available for the exhibition, and the Center reserves the right to rescind an invitation and award if it is not. At least three of the works chosen for the show must be for sale, on a 60/40 commission split in the artist's favour. Artists must attend the opening reception and artist talks on 14 November and be available to help install between 11 and 13 November; anyone who would rather the Center installed their work must drop it off on 9 or 10 November between 9am and 4pm. The Center does not ship or transport work under any circumstances, so delivery and collection are the artist's responsibility - in practice this is a call for artists who can get to the Philadelphia Main Line in person. Entry is $35 and applications go through SlideRoom. Winning artists are notified by Monday 5 October 2026. Main Line Art Center has been running since 1937 and also operates Accessible Art programmes for children and adults with disabilities; it notes separately that it does not accept unsolicited exhibition proposals and does not rent its galleries. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Verdant Fund Project Grant 2026
item.description: Grants of up to $7,000, from a pool of $60,000 dispersed each year, for non-traditional, public-facing visual art projects made in Alabama by Alabama-based artists. The Verdant Fund is the state's Andy Warhol Foundation Regional Regranting programme, administered jointly by Alabama Contemporary Art Center, the Coleman Center for the Arts and Space One Eleven, and it funds nine to fourteen projects a year. Projects must be artist-driven, happen outside traditional venues such as museums, galleries and art centres, and include a public-facing component that engages the local community - the fund's own examples include billboards and other interventions in public space, site-specific installation in non-art venues, artist books, zines and short-run publications with free public access, socially engaged and civic-practice work, moving image or new media grounded in visual arts, and dialogue-driven practices such as podcasts, research and art journalism. No medium is enumerated, and the fund's own 2026 roster answers the question directly: three of the funded projects are photographic - Didimos Johnson Pulikkottil's Camp Hill, 2030, described as a documentary photography and storytelling project shown as an open-air exhibition across a rural town; Elizabeth Ward's Under the Magnolia Trees, preserving elders' stories through film, photography and audio; and Miriam Omura's The Missing Catalog, a mobile analog archive of long-term missing persons using film photography. What the fund does not support is work that is primarily narrative or documentary film, performing arts, product design or architecture, projects inside an institution's regular programming, and anything accessible only behind a paywall. The lead applicant must reside in Alabama and keep a permanent address in the state, and must have a professional documented practice; proposals from women artists, artists of colour, artists with disabilities, LGBTQ+ artists and artists working in or from rural Alabama are prioritised. Artist compensation is a stated goal - the fund publishes recommended honorariums and says projects without them will be less competitive. Applications are free, filed through Submittable with up to seven work samples, and reviewed by a panel of three jurors drawn from regional and national artists, curators and arts professionals; the three partner organisations do not select awardees. Applications opened August 10, close October 9, 2026, notifications go out in December 2026, and funded projects may begin from January 2027 and must be complete by December 2027. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $7,000.

item.title: Life Framer — Youth
item.description: The November round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly award, judged by Matthieu Paley, the French documentary photographer whose immersive, long-term work across Central and South Asia - Mongolia, Afghanistan, China, India, Sri Lanka - has been published in National Geographic and recognised by World Press Photo and Pictures of the Year International. The brief opens with F. Scott Fitzgerald - “Youth is a dream, a form of chemical madness” - and asks for a scene or a detail that shows the habits, experiences or behaviour of the young: dreams, fears, freedom, experimentation, play, from birth through toddler, child, teen and pre-adult. Portraiture, studio, candid, conceptual, documentary and street work are all welcome, from any perspective, with images new or drawn from the archive. Life Framer accepts all types of photography from analog and digital devices including mobile phones, and allows editing, post-processing, mixed media, collage and compositing provided photography is at the heart of the work; artificial intelligence and AI-generated imagery are not accepted. Entry is tiered: $20 for one image, $30 for three, $40 for six, or $100 for a twelve-month membership allowing up to ten images in every monthly theme. The monthly first prize is $2,000, part of a $24,000 annual fund shared between the twelve monthly first-prize photographers, and the first- and second-prize photographers each month have their image exhibited in galleries around the world. Photographers retain full and exclusive rights to their work, and Life Framer aims to announce each shortlist and set of winners within fourteen days of the close date. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: ULTRASOUND · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Music moves through us the way weather moves through a landscape, the Griffin Museum writes: sudden, physical, impossible to ignore. A song can stop you mid-step; a bass line can thump through your chest before you register the words. We feel music before we understand it, and it changes the shape of a room, a car, a kitchen, a whole afternoon, the moment it starts to play. We cannot see sound itself, but we can see its effects, traces, frequencies and translations. ULTRASOUND is an online exhibition that aims to capture what happens when music takes hold, making the invisible perceptible through visual form: the dance floor mid-song, the solitary drive with the windows down, the shoulders that drop when the right track comes on, the crowd moving as one body. The museum asks for the moment music turns a body into motion, a room into a mood, a stranger into a familiar face across a crowd - what music does, not just where it happens. The online exhibition runs November 15 to December 15, 2026. It sits in the Griffin Museum's 2026 Online Exhibition Program, which puts out a new open call each quarter on themes drawn from the museum's own exhibition schedule. Entry is free, global and open to anyone - the museum states plainly that 'our online exhibitions are always free of entry, global and open'. Submissions go through a Google Form; files must be sRGB JPGs sized between 1200 and 2000 pixels on the longest side and under 1.2 MB, or they are automatically disqualified. Work is reviewed by the museum's in-house team of museum professionals and curators, with final selection by Executive Director Crista Dix. Recent online calls have drawn between 200 and 400 submissions. Selected artists get a social media package ahead of the opening, and some shows generate guest-juror Critic's Picks or artist Q&As. Copyright stays with the artist throughout. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Matriarchy Now — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by the photographer Reka Nyari, opening November 6, 2026. Matriarchy Now invites artists to explore the power, presence and complexity of women who lead - in their families, communities and beyond - and asks for work that makes us feel the weight and the grace of feminine leadership in its many forms: inherited, earned, unsung or unapologetic. SaveArtSpace frames it as a call to witness the women who have always been shaping the world and to hold them in the frame they finally deserve, and invites artists to imagine a world ruled by women, not as a mirror of the world we know but as something altogether different - where leadership is not about dominance or hierarchy but about creating the conditions for life to thrive, where family and nature sit at the centre, and where strength is measured not by who is subdued but by who is protected. The application form gives the theme as Women's Rights, Empowerment and Equality and says all art will be accepted. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; all art is accepted except corporate logos, personal advertising and video, and still JPEGs only, so photographic work is eligible. Submissions run August 31 to September 28, 2026, selected artists are announced after October 12, and the work goes up on NYC ad space from November 6 for at least one month. The potential billboard panel is 11 feet wide by 5 feet high, though the artwork itself can be any size. Up to ten images may be uploaded, at 2 MB each, with high-resolution files requested from selected artists. SaveArtSpace is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations that pay for the ad space. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: SELF · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition from Decagon Gallery calling for self portraits that go beyond likeness — images made in the act of looking at oneself honestly, uncomfortably, tenderly or strangely, rather than vanity or performance. The brief welcomes work engaging with identity, aging, illness, grief, joy, gender, memory, solitude, family, transformation and the body, staged or unstaged, constructed or straightforward, as single images or series; what matters is that the work carries real emotional stakes and that the artist was willing to be seen. Juried by Douglas Beasley, whose own practice explores the spiritual and emotional aspects of people and place and how the sacred is recognised in everyday life. Selected photographs are shown in a curated online exhibition, published in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, and accompanied by digital badges and certificates. Open to photographers worldwide; all photographic processes and styles welcome. First place receives $500, second $250, third $150 and two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total in cash awards — plus a Human Presence Award granting free entry to a future exhibition. Entry is $25 for up to 4 photographs, $5 each additional. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: HIGH 5: HUMANS · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Short-format open call from Decagon Gallery, open for only two weeks. HIGH 5 asks for a single photograph for $5, and each paid submission includes one free invitation for another photographer to enter (invited submissions do not carry a further invitation). The theme is HUMANS: photographs where human presence matters — a face, a body, a gesture, a relationship, a private moment, a chance encounter, or something harder to name. Portraits, street photography, documentary work, self-portraits, staged photography, family photographs and experimental approaches are all welcome; the person does not need to be fully visible and the photograph does not need to explain who they are. The gallery is simply looking for images that make you feel there is someone there. Open internationally to photographers 18 and over. Selected photographs are presented in the HUMANS online exhibition, on view 30 September – 31 October 2026, and one photograph is chosen as the winner, earning that photographer five free entries to future Decagon Gallery open calls. Notification is 21 September. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Darkness · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe for the photograph that lives in the low light, in the quiet spaces between heartbeats — images that know the weight of an unlit room, portraits of the unseen, landscapes of the hour before dawn, still lifes of the barely visible, reckonings with the void through the lens. The gallery wants work that finds its power not in spite of the dark but because of it. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images for the gallery walls. The gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4,500px on the longest side). Exhibition runs 1–29 January 2027 with an opening reception on 1 January; prints are archived in the gallery's flat files for six months afterwards, photographers retain all rights, and sales split 50/50. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. — Deadline: November 26, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist Residency — July–December 2027 · Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts
item.description: Kimmel Harding Nelson awards up to seventy-eight juried residencies a year to visual artists, writers, composers and interdisciplinary artists from across the United States and abroad, and this deadline fills the 2027 Session 2 window, July 12 to December 17 2027. Residencies run two to eight weeks and are entirely self-directed. Each resident gets a private bedroom and bathroom, a private studio and a $175 weekly stipend; writers and visual artists usually share an apartment with one other resident. Travel is the artist's own cost except the $100 cab fare from Omaha or Lincoln on arrival and departure, which the Kimmel Foundation pays. Selection is by a blind jury of external professionals who see only anonymous work samples and two anonymous statements — a statement of submitted works and a statement of intent — so names, credits, awards, universities, employers and gallery names must be stripped from every file. The work-sample guidelines state that "all types of visual art are accepted including but not limited to photography, painting, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, mixed media, video, performance, drawing, or textiles", with the caveat that KHN does not hold facilities specific to every process. A number of "transitional" residencies are reserved for artists within two years of the application deadline, and a number are reserved each year for Nebraska artists. The $35 application fee cannot be waived. The application portal opens November 1 2026; results are emailed by May 1 2027. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: 2–8 week residency + $175/week stipend.

item.title: Abstract II — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: The second edition of Carlotta Gallery's Abstract call - a virtual exhibition and collection centred, in the gallery's words, on "artists who approach abstraction with a distinct point of view". For Abstract II the gallery says it is interested in work that feels resolved, intentional and visually engaging, and that the selection focuses on artists who bring a personal perspective to abstraction and approach the form in a way that feels distinctive rather than familiar. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for six to twelve months, permanently featured on the gallery's Collections page with a biography and artist statement, posted to @carlottagallery, and included in a free PDF exhibition catalogue, with a Certificate of Recognition. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over; submit up to three JPEGs by email with a short biography and artist statement. — Deadline: November 10, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: North America — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition on North America - "vast, restless, and difficult to define", a place of extremes where immense distances can separate lives that exist side by side. The gallery notes that the landscape changes constantly while certain images of North America remain familiar, shaping how the place is understood both from within and from afar, and that there is always a tension between the North America that is imagined and the North America that is lived: photography can enter that space and reveal somewhere more complex, unexpected and unfinished than the pictures that usually represent it. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for six to twelve months, permanently featured on the gallery's Collections page with a biography and artist statement, posted to @carlottagallery, and included in a free PDF exhibition catalogue, with a Certificate of Recognition. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over; submit up to three JPEGs by email with a short biography and artist statement. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Emerging Global · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: The first edition of Emerging Global, Fotografiska Emerging's recurring international group exhibition, which connects the platform's global open call with Fotografiska's museum programme and rotates between Fotografiska museums. The inaugural show opens at Fotografiska Berlin in February 2027 and asks what a more conscious world means to you: Fotografiska is looking for photographic projects that explore living with greater awareness of ourselves, of one another, of the systems we are part of and of our relationship with the planet, and says it wants honest, raw and courageous work that connects personal experience with wider social and political realities. Suggested - explicitly not exclusive - themes run from climate change and our relationship with the environment to inequality and threats to human rights, consumption and waste, technology and data, community and collective action, speculative futures, and identity and belonging. Documentary, conceptual, staged, archival and experimental approaches are all welcome; the focus is on photographic, concept-driven series, though time- and prompt-based work can also be submitted. Selected artists take part in the Berlin exhibition with production and associated costs covered and organised by Fotografiska, receive an artist fee of €500, and get media and press opportunities plus visibility across Fotografiska's global channels. Entry is free; submit a header image, project title and short summary plus a PDF with at least eight images from one series, a project description and an artist CV. Up to three projects per person. A jury drawn from the Fotografiska Berlin team decides by 15 November 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Fabula Works — Lines
item.description: New open call from the Rome curatorial platform Fabula Works, themed Lines. Two photographers are selected for the first exhibition of 2027 at Millepiani in Rome (29 January – 31 March 2027, opening reception 29 January at 6pm), with printing and exhibition promotion fully covered; the organiser reserves the right to present a solo show where one submission shows a singular vision. Guest juror is Eric Bouvet, the French photojournalist and VII Foundation member, five-time World Press Photo winner and two-time Visa d'Or News recipient. All genres are welcome; the call wants photographs that make you look twice and create their own visual logic. Submit 10–25 photographs made within the last ten years as a single PDF with a biography and artist statement, in English or French; a non-refundable €25 contribution is paid via PayPal before completing the form. Open to anyone aged 18 or over, from any country. Fully AI-generated images are not allowed, though AI-assisted retouching of your own photographs is permitted. Selected photographers are contacted around six weeks before the opening. Deadline Sunday 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Southern Gothic: Artists Working Below the Mason-Dixon · NOT REAL ART
item.description: Southern Gothic is a curated virtual exhibition in NOT REAL ART's First Fridays series, online from 6 November to 31 December 2026 and featuring artists from, inspired by, or transplanted to the American South. Curated by Kirsten Bengtson-Lykoudis, a former New York gallery director and photographer now based in Richmond, Virginia, with editor-in-chief Morgan Laurens as co-organiser, it aims to move beyond stereotypes and present contemporary work by artists working below the Mason-Dixon line, exploring the region's contradictions of identity and place. Open to artists worldwide with a connection to the South, whether living, working, or making work about or within the region. All mediums and styles are welcome except work entirely generated by AI. Submit up to four works as high-resolution JPEGs with an artist bio and statement through the form on the organiser's site; there is no fee, and the call is also posted on EntryThingy. Applicants are also considered for a long-form interview on the NOT REAL ART platform and a guest appearance on its podcast. NOT REAL ART is a Los Angeles arts publisher and grant-maker powered by the 501(c)(3) Arterial; its submission terms grant a non-exclusive promotional licence while artists keep full copyright, and there is no payment for selection. Deadline 24 September 2026. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Hand Magazine - Winter Issue
item.description: Submit up to 5 images for the Winter issue of this international print publication built around photographic and printed media. The magazine's guidelines are unusually plain: "There is NEVER A THEME. We want variety!" and "Submissions are always open!" - the published quarterly cycle sets "Nov. 30th for the Winter issue". Any subject matter is accepted but all images must incorporate photographic or printed media, and selection is juried with no guarantee of publication. You must subscribe before submitting: single-issue rates are $15 in the US, $20 Canada/Mexico, $30 elsewhere. Especially strong fit for alternative-process and hybrid photo/print work. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$30. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 8th Annual Print Portfolio Exchange · Rosewood Arts Center
item.description: Rosewood Arts Center, the City of Kettering's arts facility just outside Dayton, Ohio, runs its 8th Annual Print Portfolio Exchange. Participants submit an edition of ten original prints and receive back a random assortment of eight original prints by other participants, plus a commemorative print made by artists at Rosewood and a booklet featuring all of the submitted prints. Of the ten prints submitted, one becomes part of Rosewood's permanent collection and one is exhibited in the Community Gallery as part of the centre's Holiday Sale and fundraiser. The call is open to all artists working in the print medium and any archival print process is acceptable - the centre's own account of the 6th Annual exchange describes a portfolio of relief, intaglio and photographic prints. Paper must measure 5 x 7 inches; prints at any other size are not eligible for the exchange. The edition must be ten identical prints, each signed, dated and numbered 1/10 to 10/10, interleaved with recycled paper, tissue paper or glassine before shipping, with titles optional and contact details welcome on the reverse. Entry is $15, or $10 for students, paid by cheque made out to the City of Kettering or by card over the phone, and the portfolio is posted to Rosewood in Kettering; Dayton-area artists may hand-deliver safely packed work. Entries postmarked by November 7, 2026 will be accepted, and the assembled portfolios are shipped to their new owners by December 15, 2026. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $15 ($10 students). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Revoke Exhibition Open Call
item.description: Revoke Photo Collective's exhibition open call is built around the word REVOKE - revocation as an act of creation, in which something is dismantled so something else can emerge. The brief invites resistance, rebellion, transformation, anger, liberation, rupture, memory, desire and reinvention, with no restrictions on interpretation; the collective says it wants personal and unexpected responses to the word. Open to artists working with photography anywhere, up to 15 images per entry. Selected works are curated by Linda Zhengova, a Czech-Chinese photographer, curator and writer whose own practice deals with representation, sexuality and trauma, into a punk exhibition in Melbourne running October 30 - November 1, 2026. The collective states plainly that this is a curated exhibition and that paying the fee does not guarantee a place in the show. Fees cover venue hire, professional printing, exhibition production and general running costs, so there is no further charge if selected - the collective prints the work and asks selected artists for high-resolution files at that point. Entry runs from A$40 for a single image to A$125 for fifteen. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: A$40–A$125 by image count. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: TRAVEL: Around the World 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International call from Grid Photo Gallery for travel photography in its widest sense - distant landscapes, dense cities, remote territories, familiar streets, cultural spaces, routes, borders, interiors, and environments shaped by movement or belonging. The theme is not limited to the act of travelling: the gallery asks for photographs that open a passage into the world and allow others to enter it through the image, conveying a strong sense of place through visual clarity, composition, atmosphere and intention. Expansive views and intimate details, iconic destinations and overlooked corners, everyday life and extreme or inhospitable environments are all welcome. Selected works are presented in a curated global online exhibition. First place is named Photographer of the Month with a profile interview, priority placement on promotional banners and posters, and a free entry in the next open call; second and third places are highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries get at least a month on the main-page exhibition and permanent online display afterwards, social media promotion, a digital certificate and a profile page linking to the photographer's website, and the top three become eligible for the Photography of the Year title. Selected works may also appear in a printed catalogue offered for sale. Entries opened September 1 and winners are announced December 1, 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €7. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Altered Climate — Artdoc Magazine Open Call · Artdoc Photography Magazine
item.description: International open call on global warming, environmental disruption, extreme weather and ecological change. Artdoc invites documentary and art photography alongside altered, abstract, experimental and constructed work, and explicitly encourages images that move beyond literal representation — translating the physical and psychological experience of environmental change through colour, distortion, fragmentation, layering or other photographic intervention. Selected work may be shown in a curated online exhibition, on the Featured Submissions page, or in an upcoming issue of the magazine, with a possible invitation to a portfolio interview. Submissions are free for Artdoc members; non-members must subscribe to reach the form. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication / online exhibition.

item.title: Leighton Artist Studio Residency: Photography 27/28 · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Self-directed residency of two to six weeks with private use of The Crich Photography Studio — a black-and-white analogue darkroom plus a digital photography setup, in a private studio with mountain views. Best suited to black-and-white film development, processing and printing, digital photography, and some alternative processes including cyanotype; there is no colour darkroom, no digital printing access and no production or technical support, and residents bring their own materials and equipment. Applicants choose preferred dates from three windows between April 5, 2027 and March 31, 2028. Open to individual creative professionals aged 18+ with a demonstrated record, a clearly defined project and proven analogue darkroom experience; domestic and international applicants welcome. Artists who attended any Leighton Studio residency in the past three years are ineligible. The Banff Centre Arts Scholarship covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals; Canadian Indigenous applicants receive full tuition, accommodation and meals. — Deadline: October 14, 2026. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost approx. CAD $1,001.39 per week after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Visual Arts — Sounding Like a Mountain · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (May 17 – June 18, 2027) built around acoustic ecology: how places sing, how memory persists in vibration, and how listening to the land can re-orient ethical and political relations. Participants explore how sound activates multiple temporalities shaped by land use, migration, ecological disruption and colonial infrastructures. Artists get individual studios, access to shared production facilities with technical staff, one-to-one faculty mentorship and studio visits, workshops and peer critique. Faculty are Xenia Benivolski, Elina Waage Mikalsen and Kathryn Yusoff. The program explicitly caters to artists working in photography alongside ceramics, digital media, painting, drawing, printmaking, papermaking, performance art, sculpture and installation. Open to individual artists or duos at any career stage, 18+, domestic and international; applicants need post-secondary training in visual arts or equivalent recognised experience. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship, which covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost CAD $4,476.78 after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Visual Arts — Embodied Making: Performance Art, Images and Objects · Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
item.description: Five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (July 5 – August 6, 2027) asking artists to think expansively about performance — how it emerges through movement, stillness, reading, listening, endurance, care and collective action — and how performance and materiality intersect, with images and forms activated and transformed through embodied interaction. Banff's landscape is treated as a collaborator, opening site-responsive and place-based work. Artists get individual studios, shared production facilities with technical staff, one-to-one faculty mentorship and studio visits, workshops and peer critique. Lead faculty are Brendan Fernandes and Claire Fleming Staples, both there for the full five weeks, with Abril Zales (Chief Curator, Museo Tamayo) joining as guest faculty July 12-23. The program explicitly caters to artists working in photography alongside ceramics, digital media, painting, drawing, printmaking, papermaking, performance art, sculpture and installation. Open to individual artists or duos at any career stage, 18+, domestic and international; applicants need post-secondary training in visual arts or equivalent recognised experience. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship, which covers tuition plus a contribution toward accommodation and meals. — Deadline: February 17, 2027. Fee: CAD $65 application fee (CAD $35 for Indigenous applicants); participant cost CAD $4,476.78 after the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Reflections · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Artspiration Frederick's first cash-and-carry exhibition, on view in the Artspiration Gallery in Frederick, Maryland from 4–20 December 2026. Artists are invited to explore the theme of reflection in nature, in memory, in the self, or in the world around us. Original work in any visual medium is welcome and photography is named outright alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, with the show seeking a diverse range of artistic voices, perspectives, techniques and subject matter. Open to visual artists 18 and older residing in the continental US; up to three pieces may be submitted and all three may be selected, and work must not have been previously exhibited at Artspiration Frederick. All work must be for sale and the gallery retains 40 percent of a sale, with two-dimensional work framed and wired for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Accepted work is dropped off 29 November to 1 December, or shipped to arrive by 30 November at the artist's cost with a return label included. The juror's notification is emailed 19 November and the artists' reception is 12 December, 3–5pm. The gallery is free, open to the public and accessible. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Emerging Perspectives Exhibition · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: The Delaplaine Arts Center's annual juried exhibition for young adult artists aged 18 to 35, created around 2021 after the centre noticed a gap in participation from that age group, and open nationally. There are no theme, size or media requirements or restrictions, and photography has shown here before - the 2026 line-up included a silver gelatin print. Work must be original in design and personal execution, made within the past two years and not previously displayed at the Delaplaine; no commercially made prints, giclees or reproductions are considered. The Delaplaine's exhibition-wide AI guidelines apply: work that is solely AI-generated is not considered, AI-assisted work is eligible where the artist's input clearly dominates, and any use of AI must be fully disclosed. Judging runs in two rounds - a remote first round through the online portal that decides acceptance, then in-person judging for the Grand Prize after installation - with the People's Choice decided by visitor ballot through the run of the show. The 2027 juror is Sarah Hempel Irani, a Frederick sculptor working in clay, bronze and stone who teaches sculpture at Frederick Community College and made the Claire McCardell statue on Carroll Creek. Awards are $500 for first place and $250 for the People's Choice. Up to three works may be entered; accepted artwork is delivered 22–28 March 2027 and the exhibition runs 3–25 April 2027, with the juror's talk and award announcement on 3 April. Wall-hanging work need not be framed but must be wired to a professional standard (no sawtooth hangers). Artists are not required to offer work for sale; on a sale the Delaplaine retains 30 percent, or 20 percent for members. — Deadline: February 21, 2027. Fee: $10 ($5 members). Prize: $500 + $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: SAGA Grants 2026 — Round 3 · Spokane Arts
item.description: The Spokane Arts Grant Awards fund arts and culture projects, programs and individual artists in the Spokane region, with requests of any amount up to $10,000 accepted three times a year; Round 3 of the 2026 cycle closes 1 October at 11:59pm and awards are announced 1 December. Spokane Arts will grant $166,000 across 2026 and has made more than a million dollars in awards since 2017. All arts disciplines are encouraged, 'including but not limited to, visual, performing, literary, audio, media arts, humanities, culinary, fashion, architecture, crafts and folk/traditional arts', and a past SAGA grant funded a twelve-page full-colour photographic insert on sixteen African Americans in Spokane for Black Lens News. Individuals apply as a working artist on a solo project - defined as someone trained in a discipline and/or self-identifying as a professional artist - and must hold permanent residency in the Spokane region through the award period; collectives and organisations apply in two separate categories. Applications are free and submitted through SmarterSelect, and each round's portal opens a month before its deadline. Projects must directly impact Spokane; reimbursements for past work, tuition that generates credit, pass-through grants and residency, travel or production costs outside the Spokane area are not funded, and applicants funded in the two previous consecutive years must sit a year out. A selection panel of five to six community members - one city arts commissioner, one Spokane Arts board member and three or four community members with arts experience - weighs artistic merit, effectiveness and community impact; the panel stays anonymous through the granting year, and past rosters are published by year. At least one work sample is required. Spokane Arts also offers one-to-one grant-writing appointments and free information sessions. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $10,000.

item.title: Exploring Muse & Meaning: A Juried Opportunity for Undergraduate Studio Arts Majors · Steffen Thomas Museum of Art
item.description: The Steffen Thomas Museum of Art is a single-artist museum in rural Morgan County, Georgia, built around the work of German-born American painter and sculptor Steffen Thomas, and this is the undergraduate strand of its College Connections programme - the sibling of the MFA-level Truth in Art show it ran earlier in 2026. The point is as much the apprenticeship as the wall space: selected students exhibit at a fine art museum while working alongside museum mentors on curating, loan forms and condition reports, art installation, exhibition promotion and public speaking. Entry is free, and the museum's own call banner limits it to undergraduate studio arts majors in Georgia. Applicants email a bio of up to 250 words, an artist statement of up to 150 words and high-resolution images of three to five works made within the past year, 2D or 3D, each labelled with title, date, dimensions and medium; no piece may exceed 72 x 60 inches or 50 pounds, and artists are responsible for transporting work to and from the museum. The top three Best in Show selections receive $500, $300 and $100. Submissions close 1 November 2026 and the exhibition opens 9 January 2027 at the museum on Bethany Road in Buckhead, about ten minutes from historic Madison. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 / $300 / $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Street Photography Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to street photography - the raw energy of a packed corner, the stark geometry of a dead-end street, and everything candid in between. Total prize pool $3,000: 1st prize $1,500, 2nd $500, 3rd $300, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Judge: Vineet Vohra, the Delhi-based street photographer who became the first Indian Leica Ambassador in 2015 and published his monograph Serendipity in 2024. Winners and finalists have their work professionally printed and presented at TIP's annual group show in London, and are featured to the platform's 985k+ Instagram and 200k+ Facebook following; every entrant receives a free online portfolio permanently hosted on the platform, and photographers retain full copyright in their own work. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3 and $45 for 6, the larger bundles saving 33% and 50% against single entries. AI-generated images are not accepted - submissions must be photography-based, with film, digital, smartphone, tintype and camera-less processes all welcome, and all post-production allowed provided the final result remains photography-based. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px on one side, maximum 10MB per image, and there is no age limit on when the pictures were taken. Competition entry is open to individuals who are at least 18 years old on the date of entry. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $3,000 pool.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: The Visual Arts Center at the Washington Pavilion is South Dakota's largest art museum, accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, with eight galleries in downtown Sioux Falls. Its Exhibition Selection Committee keeps a standing, no-deadline route into that programme: proposals are welcome from individual artists, artist groups and guest curators working in any medium or subject matter, and are reviewed on a quarterly basis, with the centre warning that it may take some time for a submission to be scheduled for review. The gallery list is worth reading before proposing - Gallery 301, at the entrance, frequently features photography exhibitions; the 5,000 sq ft Everist Gallery shows work in all media from established regional to international artists; the 1,700 sq ft Jerstad Gallery shows leading regional, national and international artists; the 400 sq ft Shultz Gallery is reserved for emerging regional artists; and the Contemporary Gallery covers digital, installation and new media. Applications go by email and consist of a cover letter summarising your artistic interests with a clear statement of exhibition intention and the galleries you would prioritise, a CV, an artist biography, an artist statement about the proposed body of work, and 10 to 20 high-resolution images at 300 dpi with identifying information for each. No fee is stated anywhere in the guidelines. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ARCHITECTURE · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: NYC4PA's international juried call ARCHITECTURE asks photographers for their vision of the built world - farm houses, split-level ranches and skyscrapers, but equally bridges, private houses, skylines, cathedral interiors, the pyramids of Mexico or the main hall of Grand Central. Whole structures and architectural detail are both welcome, and the organiser is explicit that a building need not be world famous. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers working in any medium, style or school of thought - print, image transfer, emulsion transfer, encaustic, black and white - with experimental and mixed techniques welcome; only 2-D work is eligible and jurying is blind, so no signatures or watermarks on images and no artist names in titles. $4,000 in cash awards go to ten prizewinners: a $1,100 Grand Prize, whose image is featured on the NYC4PA home page, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325 and three Third Prizes of $250, alongside 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions, all included in the NYC4PA online gallery and winners catalog with an award certificate. Images awarded an NYC4PA prize within the past two years are not eligible; images submitted and not selected may be resubmitted at any time. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $40 (first 3 images); $10 each additional. Prize: $1,100 Grand Prize.

item.title: BBA One Shot Award - Autumn 2026
item.description: The Autumn edition of BBA Gallery's single-image photography prize: one photograph, in any photographic medium or genre, from any artist over 18, with no restriction on training or nationality. A shortlist of 20 images is professionally printed and hung at BBA Gallery in Berlin with all production costs covered by the gallery and no shipping cost to the photographer, while a longlist of 50 is shown on a large digital display in the same space. The exhibition falls in the last week of October and is a full-space joint show combining the winning entries of the Summer and Autumn editions. First prize is €300 in cash alongside the exhibition, an Artsy profile and promotion across BBA's social channels and newsletter. Entry is a single JPG, PNG or HEIC file up to 3MB - the low ceiling is for jury review only, with a print-ready file requested if you are shortlisted - and further images can be added by buying extra credits inside the BBA app. Photographers retain full copyright; selected work must be available exclusively for sale through the gallery for the run of the show and three months after, on a 50/50 commission split. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: €19. Prize: €300.

item.title: 64th Annual Juried Competition · Masur Museum of Art
item.description: The Masur Museum of Art in Monroe, Louisiana has run its Annual Juried Competition since 1963, when Ida Kohlmeyer - a student of Mark Rothko - took first place and the museum bought her painting Immanence. It is the museum's longest-running tradition, and a significant share of its 500-work permanent collection, which also holds Picasso, Renoir and Rodin, has been acquired directly through it. The 64th edition is open to artists over 18 living in the United States and working in any medium, with no set theme; the museum receives 1,000-1,500 entries a year and hangs the selection for four months in its historic Main House. Awards total $3,200, with $1,000 for Best in Show, handed out at the March 11 opening reception, plus a separate $100 Best Packed award for the artist who crates their work most professionally - packing peanuts are grounds for disqualification. Accepted work may be offered for sale and the museum takes no commission on those sales. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 85 by 60 inches, three-dimensional work 84 inches tall within a 40 by 40 inch footprint and 200 pounds, and video is capped at five minutes. Entry is $10 per artwork with a minimum of two and a maximum of five, so $20 to $50, and the prospectus asks for recent work (it gives two different completion cutoffs, December 31 2023 in one place and December 31 2024 in another, so confirm with the museum). Submissions open on CaFE on October 1, 2026. This year's juror is not yet named. Artists are notified January 14, 2027, work is delivered February 22 - March 4, and the exhibition runs March 11 - May 15, 2027. One caution on timing: the prospectus gives the deadline as 11:59pm on December 16, but the CaFE portal's own closing field is set a day earlier, so treat December 15 as the safe date to submit by. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: $20–$50. Prize: $3,200 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 US Native American and Indigenous Artists Purchase Initiative · New Mexico Arts
item.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme buys artwork outright for publicly accessible buildings across the state - community centres, courthouses, libraries, healthcare facilities, chapter houses, tribal administrative offices, rest areas and senior centres among them. Of the programme's purchase initiatives this is the one open nationally, rather than to New Mexico residents only or to the six-state Southwest: the goal is to diversify the state collection by buying work from artists at every career stage, and although anyone resident in the United States may apply, special consideration goes to artists who identify as members of a Native American tribe or community. Galleries may submit on behalf of a represented artist regardless of that artist's residency, so long as the artist so identifies. All visual arts media in all genres are considered, and the programme's own artist FAQ names photography explicitly alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, textile, glass, collage and the rest; work must be durable, permanent, low-maintenance and ADA-compliant once installed, and suitable for interior or exterior display. Artists submit an artist statement and up to three images of completed work currently available for purchase, priced between $5,000 and $50,000. That price is all-inclusive - it must cover materials, labour, museum-quality framing under Plexiglas, security hangers, delivery, installation, insurance, taxes, commissions, the project plaque and written and photographic documentation - so budget accordingly. There is no entry fee. Since 1986 AIPP has placed more than 3,000 works across all 33 New Mexico counties, over $21 million paid directly to artists. Finalists are notified in November 2026; purchases are then made on a rolling basis through November 2028, and inclusion in the finalist pool does not guarantee a sale. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$50,000 purchase.

item.title: OPEN ECO 2026 · Photo Fringe
item.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led Brighton charity (registered no. 1148109) that has run an open-platform photography festival since 2003. OPEN ECO 2026 is an exhibition opportunity at Seafront Gallery, Brighton, on view 21 September to 12 October 2026. The organiser's call page is four lines long - venue, run dates, an 11.59pm Tuesday 15 September deadline and a link to the application form - and publishes no fee, no image count, no jury and no theme statement; the Google form needs a sign-in to open, so the 2026 brief and entry terms are visible only to applicants.
